summary: Registers a set of IANA Diameter command codes for new vendor-specific Diameter applications defined for the 3GPP Evolved Packet System. Those applications are for network elements such as the mobility management entity and the serving GPRS support node.

eli5.summary: Mobile phone networks use a messaging system whose message types need unique numbers. This note reserves those numbers for new message types used by 4G network equipment.

subtitle: Diameter codes for 3GPP mobile network equipment

tldr.problem: 3GPP (Third Generation Partnership Project) defined the Evolved Packet System, the architecture for 4G LTE networks. This system uses Diameter protocol on interfaces between the Mobile Management Entity (MME) and Home Subscriber Server (HSS), and between the Serving GPRS Support Node (SGSN) and HSS, requiring new command codes.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5516 registers nine Diameter command code pairs (codes 316–324) for the S6a/S6d application (subscriber data) and the S13/S13' application (device identity checking). These codes let network elements query and update subscriber information and verify that devices are permitted on the network.
tldr.outcome: The registered codes enable 3GPP-compliant LTE network deployments where mobile equipment, core network nodes, and authentication systems communicate using standardized Diameter messages, ensuring interoperability across vendor implementations.

today: RFC 5516 is an Informational RFC that registers Diameter codes used throughout deployed 4G LTE networks. These codes remain in active use in mobile network equipment whenever an MME, SGSN, HSS, or Equipment Identity Register communicates using Diameter for subscriber management or device verification.

sections.title: Evolved Packet System Architecture
sections.content:
The 3GPP Evolved Packet System (EPS) is the architecture for fourth-generation (4G LTE) mobile networks. Two critical network elements are the Mobile Management Entity (MME), which controls user authentication and mobility, and the Serving GPRS Support Node (SGSN), which routes data for legacy connections. Both interact with the Home Subscriber Server (HSS), which stores subscriber information like which services are allowed.

The interfaces between these elements (called S6a, S6d, S13, and S13') use the Diameter protocol. Because Diameter is extensible, each application using it needs unique command codes to avoid conflicts.
sections.eli5: In a 4G network, the phone connects to an MME, which asks the HSS if the customer is allowed on the network. They use Diameter to ask questions, but they need special codes so the answers don't get confused with other questions.

sections.title: Two Key 3GPP Applications
sections.content:
The S6a/S6d application (vendor ID 16777251) handles subscriber data. The MME or SGSN can request update-location information (commands 316), cancellation-location information (317), authentication data (318), and insertion or deletion of subscriber data (319-320). Commands for purging (321), resetting (322), and notifications (323) also transfer subscriber state.

The S13/S13' application (vendor ID 16777252) handles Mobile Equipment (ME) identity checking. The Mobile Equipment Identity Check Request/Answer (command 324) lets the MME or SGSN verify with the Equipment Identity Register that a device is not blacklisted (e.g., for theft or fraud).
sections.eli5: The S6 interface asks "what can this customer do?" The S13 interface asks "is this phone stolen or blacklisted?"

sections.title: IANA Command Code Allocations
sections.content: RFC 5516 registers nine command code values in the 3GPP vendor namespace (10415). Commands 316 through 324 are allocated as pairs (request and answer) with specific abbreviations used in 3GPP specifications. For example, code 316 handles Update-Location-Request (ULR) and Update-Location-Answer (ULA). Each command is defined in 3GPP Technical Specification TS 29.272, which provides the ABNF and semantics for the Diameter messages.
sections.eli5: IANA assigns nine numbers, one pair for each type of question the phone company needs to ask. Each number has a name like ULR (Update-Location-Request).

references.text: Calhoun, P., Loughney, J., Guttman, E., Zorn, G., and J. Arkko, "Diameter Base Protocol", RFC 3588, September 2003.
